Judgment And Award Dated 05.11.2018 Passed By The I
Addl.

SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & MACT, KALABURAGI IN MVC NO.693/2016 AND CONSEQUENTLY BE PLEASED TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FROM Rs.3,33,500/- TO Rs.15,00,000/-
WITH INTEREST @ 12% PER ANNUM FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ACTUAL REALIZATION BY FASTENING THE COMPLETE LIABILITY ON RESPONDENT NO.2 INSURANCE COMPANY, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THESE MFAs HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 14.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT

Seeking enhancement of the compensation and also to fix the liability on respondent No.2/Insurance Company, petitioners have come up with these appeals under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V.Act').
2.
Since these two appeals are arising out of a common judgment, they are clubbed together and disposed of by a common order.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioners that petitioner Chandamma is the grand mother of petitioner Sandeep.

On 27.04.2016, they along with their other relatives were traveling from Anabi village to attend a marriage function at Gawar village in auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-33/M-4351 ('offending vehicle' for short).
When they were near a bridge on Hosur-Biral Road, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in a rash or negligent manner and lost control and it turned turtle.
In the said accident, petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite taking prolonged treatment, they are not completely cured.
At the time of accident, offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.2.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and prays to allow the petitions.
5. Respondent No.1 has filed written statement denying that as on the date of accident, he was the owner of the offending vehicle and that accident occurred due to its rash or negligent driving.
He has denied the age, occupation, income, nature of the injury suffered and has sought for dismissal of the petitions.
6. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement admitting that the offending vehicle was insured with it and as on the date of accident, it was covered by a valid insurance.
It is a private car policy.
At the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving license.

Since the vehicle was used for hire or reward, there is violation of terms and conditions and as such respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition Chandamma vs Lal Mohammed Shaikh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186082506/
3 against it.
7.

sentences.text: Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
8. Petitioner Sandeep is examined as PW-1 and petitioner Chandamma as PW-2.
They have examined the Doctor, who has issued the disability certificate as PW-3.

Petitioners have relied upon Ex.P1 to 35.
9.
Respondent No.1 has examined himself as RW-1.

He has examined one Babu Ladlesab stated to be the purchaser of the offending vehicle and also the driver when the alleged accident took place as RW-2 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 4.
10.
On behalf of respondent No.2, one witness is examined as RW-3 and Ex.R5 and 6 are marked on his behalf.

11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.3,33,500/- to petitioner No.1 - Sandeep and Rs.93,100/- to petitioner No.2 - Chandamma, by holding that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 has failed to establish that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle viz., RW-2 was not holding a valid driving license.

However, on the ground that the offending vehicle is a private vehicle and it is being used for hire or reward and as such there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, it has absolved respondent No.2 from the liability of paying the compensation and directed respondent No.1 to pay the same.

It is also held that respondent No.1 is stated to have transferred the offending vehicle to RW-2 Babu Ladlesab, but having regard to the fact that the RC is not transferred to his name,
respondent No.1 continues to be the owner and as such he is liable to pay the compensation.
12.

The details of compensation granted by the Tribunal to petitioner No.1 Sandeep is as below:

 Towards injury pain and suffering 50,000  Towards medical expenses 1,12,350  Towards future medical expenses 15,000  Towards food and extra 6,400  nourishment and medical  attendant  Towards conveyance 10,000  Towards loss of income during 22,500  treatment  Permanent disability 97,200  Deprivation of future amenities 20,000  TOTAL 3,33,450  Rounded of 3,33,500 Chandamma vs Lal Mohammed Shaikh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186082506/

sentences.text:
Similarly, the details of compensation granted by the Tribunal to petitioner No.2 Chandamma is as below:
 Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Towards injury pain and suffering 40,000  Towards medical expenses 5,700  Towards food and extra 2,400  nourishment and medical  attendant  Towards conveyance 10,000  Towards loss of income during 15,000  treatment  Permanent Disability --  Deprivation of future amenities 20,000  TOTAL 93,100 14.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
15. However, petitioners have come up with these two appeals contending that the compensation granted on various heads is on lower side.

The Tribunal has erred in holding that there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and as such respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to allow the appeals, enhance the compensation and also direct respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.
16.
Heard arguments and perused the record.
17. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for petitioners and respondent No.2 reiterated the respective contentions.

They made a submission that if ultimately, this Court also comes to the conclusion that there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, at least an order for pay and recovery may be made directing respondent No.2 to pay the compensation and recover the same from respondent No.1.

However, learned counsel for respondent No.1 submits that having taken comprehensive policy, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and it cannot be permitted to recover the same from respondent No.1.
18.

Though respondent No.2 has taken up a specific defence that at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing a valid driving license, it has not led any evidence to establish the same.

In fact RW-2 who is the driver of the offending vehicle has not been cross- examined on behalf of respondent No.2 that at the time of accident, he was not possessing a valid driving license, consequently, it has failed to prove the said fact.
19. As rightly held by the Tribunal, having issued a comprehensive policy covering the risk of eight persons traveling in the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 cannot shirk its liability.

sentences.text:
Though respondent No.1 who is examined as RW-1 and RW-2 who is the purchaser of the offending vehicle have in unequivocal terms deposed and concede the fact that there was transfer of offending vehicle from Respondent No.1 to RW-2, the fact remains that Form No.29 and 30 is not exchanged between them and consequently the RC could not be transferred in the name of RW-2.
Therefore, for all practical purposes respondent No.1 remains the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he cannot claim that as on the date of accident, he was not the owner of the offending vehicle.

It appears RW-2 failed to pay the sale consideration, respondent No.1 did not chose to issue Form No.29 and 30 in his favour and therefore RW-2 could not get the offending vehicle transferred in his name.
Anyhow, having regard to the fact that RC is still standing in the name of respondent No.1, he is the owner of the offending vehicle.
21. During the course of his evidence, RW-2 has deposed that as a neighbour, he was taking petitioners and others in the offending vehicle on courtesy and the vehicle was not being on hire purpose.

However, during the course of their cross-examination, both PW-1 and 2 have in unequivocal terms deposed that at the time of accident they had taken the offending vehicle on hire and they were traveling to attend a marriage function.
This piece of evidence of PW-1 and 2 prove that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was used for hire purpose.
Since the offending vehicle is a private vehicle and it was issued with a private car policy, it was not supposed to be used for hire purpose.

Therefore, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and for this reason and having issued a comprehensive policy covering the risk of eight persons, though respondent No.2/Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation, it is entitled to recover the same from respondent No.1 for violation of terms and conditions of policy.
To this extent the impugned judgment and award is liable to be modified.
22. Now coming to the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal in favour of petitioners.

Taking into consideration the age, occupation, nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioners, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.3,33,500/- in favour of petitioner Sandeep and a sum of Rs.93,100/- in favour of petitioner Chandamma.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that the compensation granted is just and reasonable and it requires no interference by this Court and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following ORDER (i) Both appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award of the Tribunal so  far as quantum of compensation is  confirmed.
 (iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance Company is  directed to pay the compensation and Chandamma vs Lal Mohammed Shaikh And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186082506/
6 recover the same from respondent No.1.
